newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia, IMF to mull '97 programme, delayed money.
newsitem.headline: Russia, IMF to mull '97 programme, delayed money.

text.p: An International Monetary Fund mission will focus on Russia's 1997 programme during its current visit, but will also touch on the problem of delayed tranches, Russian government sources said on Tuesday.
"We shall mainly discuss the 1997 programme, which is not fully agreed upon yet," Finance Ministry macroeconomic department head Anton Siluanov told Reuters.

He said the talks would also touch upon tranches due in Janaury and February tranches from the IMF's $10 billion loan to Russia, which had been delayed because of IMF worries about tax revenues and the course of structural reforms.
Structural reforms will be one of the issues of the talks, said Larisa Zelkova, a spokeswoman for First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin.
"Questions about measures on structural reforms, including those on natural monopolies will be under discussion," she said.
President Boris Yeltsin last week slammed monopolies, including national power company Unified Energy System (UES) and gas monopoly Gazprom, for unjustifiably high prices.
Yuri Agafonov, deputy head of the economic reform department at the Economy Ministry, said there were differences of opinion between the IMF, companies and the government.
"The natural monopolies do not want to lose their privileges," he said.
He also said the IMF wanted to bring foreign consultants into the privatisation process, but Russia opposed this.
"We do not want foreign consultants, we do not understand what it means," he said.
